newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks edge up, market awaits Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks edge up, market awaits Wall Street.

text.p: Mexican stocks were marginally ahead in the early minutes on Monday after zigzagging at light trade while the market awaited developments on Wall Street, dealers said.
"It's a typical slow Monday start. Few blue chips have opened and they seem to be waiting to see how far the Dow (Jones) will slide," a floor trader said.

The leading IPC share index .MXX was up 1.88 points, or 0.04 percent, at 4,246.51. One single cross trade accounted for 11.9 million shares traded, out of an early total volume .TV.MX of 12.9 million.
Meanwhile, the Dow Jones industrial average was down 26.69 points to 7,755.35.
Dealers said telecomms firm Telmex did most to shore up the market, up 4 centavos to 18.94 pesos, followed by retail stock Cifra, up 4 centavos to 14.02 pesos.

Dealers also noted an advance in financial stock Bancomer, which was up 6 centavos to 3.76 pesos, and said the financials had gained in recent sessions on speculation of a forthcoming government program to restructure banks' past-due loans portfolios.
"There's no real market trend yet, volume is just too thin," the floor trader added.
On the broad market, of 20 stocks traded, gainers slightly outnumbered sliders by five to four.
